subject: Mutual action playbook + streaming latency bench results — next steps & close timeline
body:
From: Aaron Mills <aaron.mills@acela.health>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
Cc: Hannah Lee <h.lee@acela.health>
Date: Fri, 10 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Mutual action plan & perf benchmarks — next steps

Hi Priya,

Thanks for the call earlier. We want the MAP to explicitly include the performance acceptance criteria for our chat flows — TTFT for first token on streaming, p50/p95/p99 latency for streaming tokens, sustained concurrency targets (150 concurrent streams), and throughput (tokens/sec). Can you send the benchmark plan and a timeline for close? Procurement will need a report for our security review.

Aaron

---
From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Aaron Mills <aaron.mills@acela.health>
Cc: Hannah Lee <h.lee@acela.health>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Mutual action plan & perf benchmarks — next steps

Aaron — attaching the MAP playbook draft and the perf evaluation plan as discussed. High level:

- Scope: conversational chat generation (max prompt + response length 4k tokens), streaming enabled
- Acceptance metrics: TTFT (first byte) p50 < 80ms, p95 < 220ms, p99 < 420ms; streaming token latency p50/p95/p99 reported separately; sustained concurrency 150 streams with 95% success; throughput target 7500 tokens/sec across pool
- Testbed: dedicated Redwood Dedicated pool (g5x2-equivalent), quantized model variant (int8) + baseline fp16 model for comparison
- Workloads: 3 canonical prompt sets (support triage, clinical summary, patient Q&A) — will include warm and cold cache runs
- Timeline: perf runs and analysis 4/13–4/16; MAP update + readout 4/18; procurement report 4/20; exec close 4/21

Attachments: acela_map_playbook_v3.pdf, concurrency-scenarios.csv, streaming-latency-testplan.md (links in body).

Next steps: Vanessa will own test execution; Marissa will draft the readout slide deck. Do you want the results broken out by model variant and region?

—Priya


---
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Apr 2027 08:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Mutual action plan & perf benchmarks — next steps

On it. I'll schedule the runs tomorrow morning (4/13) and run 3 repeat passes for warm-cache and 2 cold-cache passes. Plan for rolling concurrency ramp: 1) 0→50, 2) 50→150 (10m ramp), hold 30m, then step-down. I'll collect per-connection TTFT plus per-token streaming histograms.

I'll post raw CSVs to the shared drive; Marissa — can you draft slides that call out pass/fail vs the acceptance criteria above?

-Vanessa

---
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 16 Apr 2027 14:26:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Mutual action plan & perf benchmarks — next steps

Uploading initial readout deck (attached) and a short summary CSV. Quick highlights from the runs:
- Baseline fp16 model: TTFT p50=72ms, p95=205ms, p99=385ms at 150 concurrent streams (warm-cache)
- Quantized int8 variant: TTFT p50=88ms, p95=260ms, p99=510ms at 150 concurrent streams (warm-cache)
- Streaming per-token latency (baseline fp16) p50=18ms/token, p95=56ms/token, p99=120ms/token
- Observed tail spikes during abrupt concurrency ramps — correlates with GC/host-side scheduling on one node (investigating)

We also validated throughput: aggregate sustained tokens/sec for baseline ~7900 t/s (above target); int8 ~8200 t/s but with slightly higher TTFT tail. Detailed CSVs attached.

Marissa

From: Aaron Mills <aaron.mills@acela.health>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Mutual action plan & perf benchmarks — next steps

Thanks — useful. A couple quick asks from our side before procurement signs off:
1) Can you produce a one-page runbook that maps failure modes (tail spike, node reboots) to mitigations and fallback model selection?
2) We need the p99 TTFT for cold-cache (first run after scale-up) separately — planning to present to ops.

If you can get those by 4/20 that would be perfect.

Aaron

---
From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Aaron Mills <aaron.mills@acela.health>, Hannah Lee <h.lee@acela.health>, Procurement <procurement@acela.health>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 15:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Mutual action plan & perf benchmarks — next steps

Aaron & team — attaching the one-page runbook and the cold-cache p99 TTFT figures (see streaming_latency_p50_p95_p99_summary.pdf). Summary: cold-cache p99 TTFT (baseline fp16) = 610ms; quantized int8 cold-cache p99 = 830ms. Root cause for warm-tail spikes: transient host-side scheduling during the largest step-up; mitigation: staggered ramp and a preferential routing policy that pins heavy flows to nodes with lower system load. Fallback recommendation: if p99 exceeds SLA during scale-up, fall back to dedicated baseline fp16 until kv-cache warms (this results in slightly higher throughput cost but lower TTFT tail).

Procurement — please find the MAP playbook, test artifacts, and the one-page runbook attached for your security and ops review. Happy to hop on a short call 4/21 for final Q&A.

Thanks,
Priya
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
priya_natarajan@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123
